title: Marketplace mini-launch playbook and tile copy lab
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact, practical playbook for small launches (SMB-first partners and pilot listings) — focused on the minimum required items to get a tile live + a short bank of UX microcopy and brief QA steps. Meant to be used by Solutions, Partner PM, and the launch squad as a checklist and copy reference.

Goals:
- Reduce friction: give engineering/legal a single page of what we need.
- Provide microcopy variants for product tiles, short descriptions, and trial CTAs.
- Define a light technical acceptance and privacy/security checklist for Partner listings.

Quick TL;DR checklist (single-column, must-pass items):
1) Publisher registration completed (proof of org and primary contact)
2) Product tile imagery: 1 hero 1024x512 + 3 screenshots 16:9 (1200x675 recommended)
3) Short description <= 140 chars, long description <= 800 chars (markdown ok)
4) Trial/billing gating plan documented (trial length, billing SKU mapping)
5) Security & privacy checklist signed off by security (KMS, PII handling, SOC/ISO claims)
6) Integration artifacts: API endpoint, sample request, rate limit expectations, auth scheme (OAuth2/API key)
7) License/terms sample and data processing addendum (DPA) included
8) Launch owner (Partner PM) + SRE on-call for first 72 hours

Tile and microcopy lab (pick one from each group and tweak):
- 6–word hero headline options (short):
  • "Fast, predictable LLM inference — Redwood-backed"
  • "Serve LLMs at scale with cost controls"
  • "Low-latency text + embeddings, production-ready"

- Short description (one-line, for marketplace tile):
  • Option A: "Hosted LLM inference with predictable latency, cost controls, and one-click deployment."
  • Option B: "Redwood Inference: production-grade text generation, embeddings, and routing across clouds."
  • Option C: "High-throughput inference for developers — autoscaling, caching, and observability."

- 140-char trial CTA variants:
  • "Start a 14-day free trial — no card required."
  • "Try Redwood in your account: 7-day trial, easiest onboarding for inference."
  • "Launch a pilot cluster — free trial credits and onboarding help."

- Long description (core bullets to include, reorder as needed):
  • What it is: Redwood Inference provides a unified runtime for serving LLMs with predictable latency and cost.
  • Key features: Streaming generation, embeddings, model catalog, autoscaling, KV/prefix caching.
  • Security & deployment modes: Hosted, Dedicated, Private (VPC/on-prem).
  • Who it's for: Platform teams, product engineers, regulated customers.
  • Getting started: link to quickstart, sample requests, SDK snippets.

UX placement guidance (tile → details page → trial flow):
- Tile shows hero headline + 1-line description + badges: "SLA available", "Private deployment", "Free trial".
- Details page should include: 1) short demo GIF (15–30s of interface or console), 2) architecture diagram, 3) quickstart code snippet for text generation in two languages, 4) pricing summary and billing link.
- Trial flow: self-serve box to request trial credits for trial partner accounts; if requesting Dedicated, route to partnership team (manual step).

Technical acceptance checklist (light):
- API smoke test: successful generation (<= 1s P50 on small prompt) from partner staging endpoint (provide sample prompt).
- Auth: token exchange / bearer token flow validated; secrets handling documented.
- Observability: partner exposes metrics or integrates with our tracing hooks (span names, request ids).
- Rate limits: documented expected qps and burst allowances.
- Rollback plan: documented fallback (alternate model or degrade to cached responses).

Security & privacy quick gate (must confirm or provide mitigation):
- Data residency & retention: state whether customer data is stored, cached, or kept in KV cache; retention TTL.
- Encryption: TLS in transit, KMS usage for at-rest keys if storing customer data.
- PII processing: flag if partner processes PII and provide DPA or minimal redaction plan.
- Compliance statements: list if partner claims SOC2/ISO27001 or other; attach attestation.

Billing & SKU mapping (practical steps):
1) Decide plan type: metered per-token, flat monthly seat, or reserved capacity SKU.
2) Map marketplace SKU to Redwood product SKU (example mapping: marketplace.SMB.basic -> redwood.hosted.provisioned.sku.small).
3) Define trial credit amount and how credits convert to usage.
4) Add usage metering endpoints and sample CSV export for marketplace reconciliation.

Screenshot & asset checklist (deliverables to collect from partner):
- hero-image.png 1024x512 (transparent background ok)
- three screenshots (web console or sample output) 1200x675
- short logo svg + png (256px)
- 1 animated GIF demo (<= 15s, annotated)

Launch timeline (mini-sprint, 2 weeks typical for light listing):
- Day 0: Asset intake, publisher verification, tile copy draft (owner: Partner PM)
- Day 1–3: Security/Legal review, SKU mapping (owner: Security, Finance)
- Day 4–7: Engineering smoke tests + observability hooks (owner: Eng squad)
- Day 8–10: Marketplace QA and screenshots validation (owner: Launch QA)
- Day 11–14: Publish, small PR push, monitor first 72 hours (owner: Partner PM + SRE)

Monitoring & post-launch playbook (first 72 hours):
- SRE = on-call for first 72 hours; check latency and error rate thrice daily and on alerts.
- Usage & cost: Finance reviews early usage for misbilling or runaway costs; set emergency throttles.
- Customer feedback: enable an in-tile contact link and have Solutions lead triage responses.

Open questions / decisions to make (TODOs):
- Trial length default: 7 or 14 days? (ops & growth decision)
- Auto-conversion after trial: send 3 email reminders or 1 in-product nudge?
- Who is authorized to approve Dedicated pilot capacity for small partners?

Slack/Confluence/Jira snippets to use when coordinating launch:
- Slack shorthand: #marketplace-launches, tag @oncall-sre + @sales-ops for go/no-go.
- Confluence page template: "Marketplace Launch — <partner-name> — <date>" (include checklist table and asset links).
- Jira epic template: MARKETPLACE-<partner> with sub-tasks: assets, security, engineering, billing, QA, publish.

Minimal sample tile copy (final-ready draft):
- Headline: "Production LLM inference — low latency, lower cost"
- One-line: "Deploy Redwood-powered inference with autoscaling, caching, and clear billing — ready for production."
- CTA button: "Start free trial" (secondary: "Contact sales")

Sign-off section (who signs, recommended):
- Go/no-go signers: Partner PM, Security lead, Finance rep, Engineering owner.
- Record approvals in Confluence and attach legal DPA.

Notes to self / rough edits (working):
- Consider a "sandbox" SKU for developer testing that has very low cost but throttled throughput.
- Include example prompts that demonstrate token counts for common tasks (summarization, Q&A, embeddings).
- Reach out to Growth for suggested A/B microcopy experiments for CTA language.

If you're the owner: use this file as the single source of truth for the initial intake. Replace placeholders with links and mark checklist items as done inline in the Confluence launch page.

Document history:
- 2025-02-15 created by Aisha Patel (initial draft)
- 2025-02-20 added microcopy variants and technical acceptance items (Liam Chen)
- 2025-03-01 updated rollout timeline and added billing SKU mapping note (Sofia Martinez)

End of doc.
